Residual_sea_ice and Residual_cloud_water are correlated (r ≈ -0.14), so D is unlikely. The data alone don't settle the direction, so I chose it on physical grounds. Less sea ice exposes more open water, which adds moisture and heat to the air and raises cloud water. Cloud water also influences sea ice, but the link from ice to clouds is the stronger and better documented one in Arctic studies. That points to B. I didn't run a causal discovery test, so this rests on that reasoning plus the correlation.

ANSWER: B
